theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What does a semi-permanent colour do to the hair?
options: It lightens the client's natural colour by several levels
It changes the hair's natural curl pattern as well as its colour
It adds colour without lifting, and fades over some shampoos
It colours the new growth so that it grows out in the same shade

questions.stem: Where do most semi-permanent colour molecules sit in the hair?
options: Deep in the medulla, at the very centre of the hair
In the skin of the scalp, around the hair root
In and just under the cuticle, the outer layer
Only on the surface of the scalp

questions.stem: Why does semi-permanent colour fade little by little?
options: It is only a coloured powder that blows off in the breeze
Sunlight slowly turns it into a permanent colour in the hair
The developer mixed into it keeps working on the hair for weeks
Its molecules are small enough to wash slowly out of the hair

questions.stem: How is semi-permanent colour different from permanent colour?
options: It lightens the hair more and lasts much longer
It cannot lighten hair and does not last until cut
It always needs a strong developer mixed in every time
It must always be applied to dry hair, never damp

questions.stem: How is semi-permanent colour different from temporary colour (such as a colour rinse or spray)?
options: Semi-permanent washes out in one shampoo; temporary lasts for weeks
Semi-permanent enters the hair a little; temporary only coats it
Temporary colour needs a skin test; semi-permanent never does
Temporary colour can lighten hair; semi-permanent cannot

questions.stem: Which client is the best match for a semi-permanent colour?
options: Kemar, who wants his black hair to turn a pale platinum blonde
Marcia, who wants to lift her hair three whole levels lighter
Jodi-Ann, who wants richer tone and shine on dark hair
Sashana, who wants a colour that never fades or grows out

questions.stem: Why do some clients choose semi-permanent colour to blend a little grey?
options: It turns grey hair back to its own natural colour for good
It lifts the grey hair to match the rest of the hair
It stops any more grey hairs from growing out of the scalp
It softens grey and fades with no hard regrowth line

questions.stem: Which result can a semi-permanent colour give?
options: Only a shade lighter than the natural colour
The same level as the hair, or darker
Any shade, as long as it is left on longer
Only black, because it cannot make other shades

questions.stem: Odane has level 2 (very dark) hair and wants a bright red semi-permanent. What will he most likely see?
options: Bright red hair all over, the same as the colour chart
Hair that is lighter than before, with a red tone
Only a slight red tint, seen mostly in strong light
Green hair, because red and dark hair do not mix

questions.stem: Does a semi-permanent colour need to be mixed with a developer?
options: Yes, it must always be mixed with the strongest developer in stock
Yes, with bleach, so that the colour can enter the hair
No, but it must be mixed with a perm lotion
Most do not; some deposit-only colours use a low-strength one

questions.stem: Does semi-permanent colour need a skin test?
options: No, because semi-permanent colour has no chemicals in it at all
Yes, when the maker says so, because it can still cause allergy
No, because it washes out after a few shampoos
Only if the client has very fine or light-coloured hair

questions.stem: Why do a strand test before a semi-permanent colour on porous hair?
options: To find out whether the client is allergic to the colour
To check the client's natural curl pattern before colouring
To see if porous parts take the colour darker
To measure how fast the client's hair grows each month

questions.stem: Why do you ask a client what she has put on her hair in the last few months?
options: Past colour, henna or relaxer can change how the colour takes
So that you can tell her which brand of shampoo to buy next
So that you can charge her for the products she used before
Because past products make the skin test unnecessary for her

questions.stem: Which of these is a reason to put off the colour service until another day?
options: The client has dark hair and wants a richer tone
The client has a sore, weeping area on her scalp
The client had a trim two weeks ago
The client wants to blend a few grey hairs

questions.stem: For most semi-permanent colours, how should the hair be prepared before application?
options: Left with all styling products on, to help hold the colour
Shampooed and towel-dried, unless the maker says otherwise
Pressed straight with a hot comb first so the colour lies flat
Soaked with heavy conditioner so the colour slides on easily

questions.stem: Why is a heavy conditioner usually not used just before a semi-permanent colour?
options: It makes the colour come out far too bright
It turns the colour green on dark hair
It makes the client's skin test show a reaction
It can coat the hair and block the colour

questions.stem: Which tools are best for applying a semi-permanent colour?
options: A metal bowl and a stiff wire brush from the hardware store
A hot pressing comb and a natural bristle brush
A razor and a fine cutting comb for parting
A tint brush and a clean plastic bowl

questions.stem: Why should you wear gloves when applying a semi-permanent colour?
options: To keep the colour warm while you apply it
To stop the hair from sticking to your fingers
To protect your skin from stains and allergy
So that the colour lasts longer on the client

questions.stem: How do you protect the client's skin from colour stains?
options: Apply barrier cream along the hairline and on the ears
Ask the client to hold a towel up over her face the whole time
Put the colour on very thinly near the face and ears only
Spray the hairline and ears with plenty of water first

questions.stem: How is semi-permanent colour usually applied?
options: Evenly from roots to ends, working through every section
Only on the roots, leaving the lengths and ends uncoloured
Only on the ends, leaving the roots and mid-lengths uncoloured
In a single wide stripe down the centre parting

questions.stem: Why should colour be worked through natural coily hair in small sections?
options: Coily hair takes colour too fast if the sections are large
Small sections keep the colour from staining the skin
Small sections make the colour process with less heat
Tight coils can hide hair, so large sections may be missed

questions.stem: How long should a semi-permanent colour be left on?
options: Always overnight, for the best result
Until the client's scalp feels warm
Five minutes for every grey hair
For the time the maker says

questions.stem: Some makers say to use a plastic cap or gentle heat during processing. Why?
options: To dry the colour into the hair before it is rinsed
To stop the client from seeing the colour too early
To help the colour enter the hair more evenly
To make the colour lighten the natural hair

questions.stem: How is semi-permanent colour usually removed at the end?
options: Shampooed three times with a strong clarifying shampoo
Wiped off with a dry towel and left in
Brushed out of the dry hair with a bristle brush
Rinsed until the water runs clear, as the maker says

questions.stem: Why should you not shampoo hard straight after a semi-permanent colour, unless the maker says to?
options: Shampoo turns semi-permanent colour into permanent
Shampoo makes the colour go lighter than the hair
It can wash out some of the new colour
It stops the hair from drying properly

questions.stem: A client's hair has an unwanted brassy gold tone. Which semi-permanent tone would help cancel it?
options: A violet or ash tone
A gold or copper tone
A warm red tone
An orange tone

questions.stem: Which of these are 'warm' tones in hair colour?
options: Red, copper and gold
Ash, blue and violet
Black and silver
Green and blue only

questions.stem: Which colour is made by mixing blue and yellow?
options: Orange
Green
Violet
Red

questions.stem: Why may the ends of long relaxed hair turn out darker than the roots after a semi-permanent colour?
options: The ends are the newest hair, so they grab the most colour
The roots get less colour because they are wet
The ends are more porous, so they take in more colour
The ends were rinsed with hotter water

questions.stem: Why is semi-permanent colour often a good choice for a client trying colour for the first time?
options: It fades away over time, so it is not a long commitment
It is the only colour that never needs a skin test
It lightens the hair so the client can see a big change
It changes the curl pattern so the client can try a new look

questions.stem: How can semi-permanent colour help a client whose permanent colour has faded on the ends?
options: It lifts the faded ends back to a lighter shade
It removes the old colour so the hair is natural again
It adds tone back to the faded lengths and ends
It makes the regrowth at the roots stop showing

questions.stem: Why is semi-permanent colour often gentle on natural textured hair?
options: Most types contain no ammonia and do not lift the hair
It straightens the coils a little while it colours the hair
It is always made only from plants, with no chemicals at all
It adds new protein that makes the hair grow

questions.stem: Why should the salon be well ventilated during colour services?
options: To clear product fumes so that nobody breathes them in
To make the colour on the client process much faster
To stop the colour from dripping and staining the floor
To keep the tint brushes and bowls dry between clients

questions.stem: Colour splashes onto a client's face (not the eyes). What should you do?
options: Leave it until the service is finished, then scrub it
Rub it with a dry towel until the skin is red
Wipe it off at once with damp cotton wool
Cover it with powder so it cannot be seen

questions.stem: How should opened bottles of semi-permanent colour be stored?
options: With the caps left off so that the colour can breathe
In a sunny window so they stay warm
Capped tightly, in a cool, dark place, labelled
Mixed into one bottle to make a new shade

questions.stem: Colour has been poured into a bowl but not all of it was used. What should you do with the rest?
options: Throw it away as the maker and the Centre's rules say
Pour it back into the original bottle for the next client
Leave it in the bowl to use tomorrow
Mix it with the next client's permanent colour

questions.stem: Why must a fresh, clean towel be used for each client?
options: To stop germs and dirt passing from one client to the next
Because used towels make the colour process too slowly
Because colour stains will not show on a fresh towel
So that the salon can count how many towels it has at night

questions.stem: What is the difference between disinfecting and sterilising?
options: Disinfecting kills all germs and spores; sterilising removes only dirt
Disinfecting kills most germs; sterilising kills all, even spores
They mean the same thing in a salon
Sterilising is only wiping with a damp cloth

questions.stem: Which advice helps a semi-permanent colour last longer?
options: Wash the hair every day with a clarifying shampoo
Swim often without rinsing the hair after
Leave the hair in the strong sun to set the colour
Use a gentle, colour-safe shampoo and cool water

questions.stem: Kimone asks how long her semi-permanent colour will last. What is the best answer?
options: It will stay until the hair is cut off
It fades over a number of shampoos, as the maker says
It washes out completely the first time she wets it
It lasts exactly one year, whatever she does

questions.stem: When checking the finished colour, what should you look for?
options: Whether the hair is lighter than the shade chart
Even colour from roots to ends, with no missed patches
Whether the scalp has turned the same colour as the hair
That the hair is still damp in the middle

questions.stem: Why should you write the shade and timing of a semi-permanent colour on the record card?
options: So that the client can be charged twice for one service
Because the salon's bank needs it for its records
So that the shade can be sold to another salon
So the result can be repeated or changed next time

questions.stem: How should the colour area be left after the service?
options: With products left open and ready for the next client
With the used towels left on the chair so they can dry
With colour spills left to dry so they are easy to scrape
Clean, with spills wiped, tools washed and disinfected

questions.stem: Which product would you suggest to help a semi-permanent colour on dry natural hair?
options: A moisturising, colour-safe conditioner
A strong clarifying shampoo for daily use
A bleach-based home lightening kit
A thick styling gel used every day

questions.stem: After rinsing, Monique says her scalp is itchy and red. What should you do?
options: Apply more colour over the red area to even out the tone
Rinse with cool water and tell the instructor at once
Tell her that it is quite normal and send her home
Put her under a hot dryer for a while to calm the scalp

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What term describes a colour that only adds colour to the hair and does not lighten it?
How many levels lighter can a semi-permanent colour make natural hair?
On the usual level system, which number stands for black?
Which secondary colour is made by mixing red and blue?
Which colour is opposite red on the colour wheel?
What is the name of the natural pigment that gives hair its colour?
What word describes how easily the hair takes in water and products?
What is the name of the squeeze bottle with a nozzle often used to apply semi-permanent colour?
What is the name of the maker's card or book of hair samples used to choose a shade?
When a maker asks for a skin test before a colour service, how many hours before is it most often done?
What do the letters PPE stand for?
What product, made for skin, is used to take colour stains off the hairline after a colour?
What colour do we call hair that has lost all its natural pigment?
Which comb, with a long thin handle, is used to divide the hair into neat sections for colouring?
What should you use to time the processing exactly?

essays.stem: Compare temporary, semi-permanent and permanent hair colour. For each, say how it works, how long it lasts, and whether it can lighten hair.
essays.modelAnswer: Temporary colour, such as a rinse, spray or mousse, only coats the outside of the hair. It does not go into the hair, it cannot lighten, and it usually washes out at the next shampoo. Semi-permanent colour has small molecules that go a little way into the hair, into and just under the cuticle. Most types need no developer and have no ammonia. It can make the hair the same level or darker, add tone and shine, and blend some grey, but it cannot lighten. It fades slowly over a number of shampoos, as the maker says, so there is no hard regrowth line. Permanent colour is mixed with a developer. Its molecules go into the cortex and join into large ones that cannot wash out. It can lighten as well as add colour, and it lasts until the hair grows out or is cut, so it needs regrowth retouches.
markingPoints: Temporary: coats the outside, no lift, washes out at the next shampoo
Semi-permanent: enters the hair a little, usually no developer or ammonia
Semi-permanent: same level or darker, cannot lighten, fades over several shampoos
Permanent: mixed with developer, molecules trapped in the cortex
Permanent: can lighten, lasts until cut, needs regrowth retouches

essays.stem: Describe the consultation and tests you would carry out before a semi-permanent colour service.
essays.modelAnswer: I ask the client what result she wants and show her the shade chart, and I explain that semi-permanent colour cannot make hair lighter and will fade over some shampoos. I ask about past services, such as relaxers, permanent colour, henna or home dyes, and about allergies or any reaction to colour before. I look at the scalp for cuts, sores, redness or infection, and if I find any, I put off the service and suggest she sees a doctor. I check her natural level in good light, how much grey she has, and the hair's porosity and condition, especially on the ends of relaxed or long hair. I carry out a skin test as the maker says, often 48 hours before, and a strand test if the hair is porous or uneven. Then I agree the shade, time and price, and write everything on the record card.
markingPoints: Agrees the result and explains that semi-permanent cannot lighten and will fade
Asks about past chemical services, henna, allergies and past reactions
Checks the scalp and puts off the service (refers) if there is a problem
Checks natural level, grey, porosity and condition
Skin test as the maker says (often 48 hours) and strand test; records everything

essays.stem: Latoya has natural level 3 hair with some unwanted brassy tones. Explain how you would choose a semi-permanent shade for her, and what result she can expect.
essays.modelAnswer: First I find Latoya's natural level, which is level 3, a dark brown, by checking dry hair against the shade chart in daylight. Because semi-permanent colour cannot lighten, I must choose a shade at level 3 or darker. A lighter shade would not show. I would explain that on dark hair a bright shade shows only as a tint, mostly in strong light. To deal with the brassy tones, I use the colour wheel. Brassy hair has orange and gold in it. Opposite colours cancel each other, so blue cancels orange and violet cancels yellow. I would choose an ash or cool shade at her level to give a richer, more natural brown. I would do a strand test, especially on porous ends, to check the result. She can expect a richer, shinier colour that fades gently over some shampoos.
markingPoints: Finds the natural level on dry hair against the shade chart
Chooses the same level or darker, because semi-permanent cannot lighten
Explains that bright shades show only as a tint on dark hair
Uses the colour wheel: ash or cool tones cancel brassy orange and gold
Strand tests, and explains the result fades over some shampoos

essays.stem: Describe the steps for applying a semi-permanent colour, from preparing the client to rinsing.
essays.modelAnswer: I check that the skin test is clear and the scalp is healthy. I put a towel and cape on the client and wear gloves and an apron. I shampoo the hair, without conditioner, and towel-dry it, unless the maker says otherwise. I put barrier cream along the hairline and on the ears. I comb the hair gently and divide it into four sections, then work in small sub-sections. I apply the colour with an applicator bottle or tint brush evenly from roots to ends, making sure every part is covered, and I gently work it through. I time it for exactly as long as the maker says, using a plastic cap or gentle heat only if the maker says to. At the end I check the colour on a strand, then rinse with lukewarm or cool water until the water runs clear. I remove any stains from the skin and finish the hair.
markingPoints: Checks skin test and scalp; gowns the client; wears gloves
Shampoos and towel-dries (as the maker says); applies barrier cream
Sections the hair and applies colour evenly from roots to ends
Times as the maker says, with heat or a cap only if the maker says
Checks a strand, rinses until clear, removes stains and finishes

essays.stem: Describe the extra care needed when giving a semi-permanent colour to natural coily hair and to relaxed hair.
essays.modelAnswer: Semi-permanent colour is often a good choice for natural and relaxed hair, because most types have no ammonia and do not lift. Natural coily hair is often dry and can break if it is combed roughly. I detangle it gently first, working from the ends up with a wide-tooth comb, and I keep tension low. The tight coils can hide parts of the hair, so I work in small sections and make sure the colour covers every hair. Relaxed hair is often porous, especially on the ends, so it can take the colour darker or unevenly. I do a strand test, and I may apply to the less porous roots first or use a shorter time on the ends, as the maker allows. I leave the time between the relaxer and the colour that the maker says. After colour, both need moisture, gentle handling and deep conditioning.
markingPoints: Notes semi-permanent is gentle (usually no ammonia, no lift)
Coily hair: detangles gently from the ends, low tension
Small sections to cover every hair in tight coils
Relaxed hair is porous: strand test, care on the ends, maker's time after a relaxer
Aftercare: moisture, gentle handling, deep conditioning

essays.stem: Describe how you would work safely with semi-permanent colour, including PPE, ventilation, first aid and storage.
essays.modelAnswer: I follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules. I wear gloves and an apron, and I protect the client with a towel, a cape and barrier cream. I keep the area well ventilated so that fumes do not build up. I never mix products from different makers. If colour gets on the skin, I wipe it off at once with damp cotton wool. If it gets in an eye, I rinse the eye straight away with plenty of clean water and get medical help. If the client says her scalp itches or burns, I rinse the colour off and tell the instructor. I wipe up spills at once so that nobody slips. I store colour with the caps on tight, labelled, in a cool, dark place away from heat, and out of reach of children. Leftover colour in a bowl is thrown away as the maker and Centre say.
markingPoints: Gloves and apron; client protected with towel, cape and barrier cream
Good ventilation; maker's instructions; never mixes brands
First aid: wipe skin; rinse eyes with plenty of clean water and get help
Stops and rinses if the scalp itches or burns, and reports it
Stores capped, labelled, cool and dark; throws away leftovers

essays.stem: Explain the difference between cleaning, disinfecting and sterilising, and how you would make the tools and towels safe for the next colour client.
essays.modelAnswer: Cleaning means removing dirt, hair and product with soap and water. It must always be done first, because a disinfectant cannot work through dirt. Disinfecting means using a chemical disinfectant, made up and timed as the maker says, to kill most germs on a cleaned surface or tool. Sterilising kills all germs, including spores, and is done with special equipment; most salon colour tools are disinfected rather than sterilised. After a colour service I wash the bowls, tint brushes, combs and clips in warm, soapy water to remove all colour and hair, rinse them, and then put them in disinfectant for the time the maker says. I dry them and store them in a clean, covered place. I wipe the trolley and chair with disinfectant. Used towels go in the laundry, and a fresh towel is used for each client. Single-use items such as neck strips are thrown away.
markingPoints: Cleaning removes dirt and must come first
Disinfecting kills most germs, using the maker's strength and time
Sterilising kills all germs, including spores
Washes, disinfects, dries and stores tools covered
Fresh towel for each client; laundry; single-use items thrown away

essays.stem: Explain why porous hair can give an uneven semi-permanent colour result, and how you would prevent this.
essays.modelAnswer: Porous hair has a raised or damaged cuticle, so it takes in liquids and colour more quickly than healthy hair. Hair is often more porous at the ends, because they are older and have had more sun, heat, combing and chemical services, such as relaxers. When semi-permanent colour is put on, the porous parts can soak up more colour and turn out darker or a different tone from the roots, so the result looks patchy. The colour may also fade faster from very porous hair. To prevent this, I check the porosity during the consultation by feeling the hair and looking at it. I do a strand test on the most porous part. Depending on the result, I may choose a lighter shade, apply to the roots first and the ends later, use a shorter time on the ends, or use a conditioning treatment first, as the maker allows.
markingPoints: Porous hair has a raised or damaged cuticle and takes in colour fast
Ends are usually most porous (age, heat, chemicals)
Porous parts can come out darker or uneven, and fade faster
Checks porosity and does a strand test
Adjusts shade, timing or order of application, or pre-treats as the maker allows

essays.stem: What aftercare advice and products would you suggest to a client after a semi-permanent colour, and why?
essays.modelAnswer: I would explain that semi-permanent colour fades a little each time the hair is washed, so how she washes it matters. She should use a gentle, colour-safe shampoo and conditioner, and rinse with cool or lukewarm water, because hot water opens the cuticle and lets colour out faster. She should not wash her hair more often than she needs to. Strong sun, sea water and pool chlorine also fade colour, so she can wear a hat or scarf in the sun and rinse after swimming. If she uses heat, she should use a heat protectant and keep the heat low. For natural or relaxed hair, a moisturising conditioner and a weekly deep treatment keep the hair soft and help the colour look shiny. She should sleep on a satin scarf or bonnet. I would suggest booking again in a few weeks to refresh the colour.
markingPoints: Explains the colour fades with washing
Colour-safe shampoo and conditioner; cool or lukewarm water; wash less often
Protect from sun, sea and chlorine; low heat with protectant
Moisture and deep conditioning for natural or relaxed hair; satin scarf
Suggests a refresh appointment

essays.stem: Describe how you would clean up after a semi-permanent colour service and what you would write on the client's record card.
essays.modelAnswer: With gloves still on, I throw away any colour left in the bowl, as the maker and the Centre's rules say, and I never pour it back into the bottle. I cap the bottles tightly, wipe them, and return them to a cool, dark store with the labels facing out. I wash the bowls, brushes, combs and clips to remove all colour and hair, then disinfect, dry and store them. I put used towels and the cape in the laundry, throw away neck strips and cotton wool, and wipe the basin, chair and trolley. I sweep up hair and mop spills so that nobody slips. On the record card I write the date, the skin test date and result, the strand test result, the shade, whether any developer was used, the processing time, any heat used, the result, and the advice and products given. This helps the next stylist repeat or adjust the colour.
markingPoints: Throws leftover colour away as the maker and Centre say
Caps, wipes and stores products correctly
Washes, disinfects and stores tools; laundry; bins single-use items; wipes surfaces
Sweeps and mops spills
Records tests, shade, time, heat, result and advice so it can be repeated

practical1.title: Semi-permanent shade test board on different hair swatches
practical1.brief: As a group, find out how semi-permanent colours behave on different hair. Set up a safe colour station. You have hair swatches of four kinds: natural dark coily hair (level 2 to 3), relaxed or porous hair, hair with grey, and a lighter swatch. Each member chooses one shade from the maker's chart, predicts the result on each kind of swatch, and writes the prediction down. Then each member shampoos and towel-dries their swatches (unless the maker says otherwise), applies the colour evenly, times it as the maker says, rinses it until the water runs clear, and dries it. Together, mount every swatch on a test board next to an uncoloured piece of the same hair, with the shade, time and prediction written beside it. Each member then explains one result to the assessor using level, tone and porosity. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Clean up and hand in the board once for the whole group.
materials: Semi-permanent colours in at least four shades from one maker
Labelled hair swatches: natural dark coily, relaxed or porous, with grey, and lighter
Gentle shampoo, towels and a basin
Plastic bowls, tint brushes or applicator bottles
Timer, card board, tape and marker pens
Disinfectant for tools, as the Centre uses
photos: The colour station set up, with products, tools and PPE laid out
The written predictions beside the uncoloured swatches
Colour being applied to the swatches
The swatches during rinsing, with the water running clear
The finished test board with all swatches labelled
The area cleaned, tools in disinfectant and products stored
checklist: Wore gloves and an apron and kept the area ventilated
Prepared the swatches as the maker says
Applied colour evenly to every part of each swatch
Timed the processing as the maker says and rinsed until clear
Labelled each swatch with the shade, time and prediction
Explained one result correctly using level, tone and porosity
Threw away leftover colour and cleaned, disinfected and stored tools
safety: Follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules; never mix brands
Wear gloves and keep the area ventilated
Wipe up spills at once so nobody slips
Rinse eyes or skin with plenty of clean water if colour touches them

practical2.title: Semi-permanent colour service on a model or practice head
practical2.brief: As a group, give a semi-permanent colour service on a model who agrees to it, or on a practice head with human hair. A model must have a clear skin test done as the maker says, and a healthy scalp. The hair can be natural, textured or relaxed. Share the work: one member leads the consultation, finds the natural level and fills in the record card; one shampoos and towel-dries the hair; one applies barrier cream and divides the hair into four sections; then each member colours one section evenly from roots to ends. One member times the processing. Members take turns to check a strand, rinse until the water runs clear, condition if the maker allows, and dry and style the hair. One member explains the aftercare to the client. Photograph each stage below, showing the hair only, never the face unless the model agrees and the Centre allows it. Hand in the record card once for the whole group.
materials: A model who agrees, or a practice head with human hair
Semi-permanent colour chosen for the client, from one maker
Applicator bottles or tint brushes and plastic bowls
Gloves, aprons, capes, towels and neck strips
Barrier cream, sectioning clips, tail comb and wide-tooth comb
Gentle shampoo, timer, and skin stain remover
photos: The record card with the skin test result (no names if the model prefers)
The hair before colouring, in four sections, with barrier cream in place
Colour being applied in small sub-sections
The full head covered with colour, before processing
The finished colour, dried and styled, from the back and side
The work area cleaned and tools in the disinfectant
checklist: Checked the skin test result and the scalp before starting
Protected the client and wore gloves and an apron
Prepared the hair as the maker says
Applied the colour evenly with no missed areas
Timed the processing as the maker says
Rinsed until clear and removed any skin stains
Gave suitable aftercare advice and helped complete the record card
Cleaned and disinfected tools and left the area safe and tidy
safety: Follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules; never mix brands
Do not colour if the skin test shows a reaction or the scalp has cuts or sores
Wear gloves and keep the area ventilated
Stop and rinse if the client's scalp itches or burns, and tell the instructor
